series.name: How It Works
series.format: One everyday machine from closed box to working principle in 35-50 s: whole object, cut it open, name the 3-4 parts that matter, run the mechanism once slowly (the hero moment), then the surprise.
series.hookFormula: Hidden-machine claim: '[Everyday thing] is secretly a [surprising thing].'
series.example: Your house key is a password. (how a pin-tumbler lock opens)

series.name: What's Inside
series.format: A sealed object you own, exploded into every part in one big fly-apart, then reassembled part by part while each one is named and its job shown. The reveal is the part nobody knew was in there.
series.example: There's a tiny radioactive source inside some smoke alarms.

series.name: Why It Doesn't Fail
series.format: Starts on the scary failure everyone imagines, then shows the design that makes it (almost) impossible: redundancy, fail-safe defaults, physics doing the work. Calm, reassuring, never alarmist.
series.hookFormula: What happens if [the scary failure]? Almost nothing, because...
series.example: What happens if an elevator's cable snaps? The car barely drops.

series.name: Tiny Machines
series.format: A mechanism smaller than your fingertip, scaled up to fill the screen. Count how many times it moves (per second, per day) and end on the number.
series.hookFormula: This [tiny part] [does something] [huge number] times a [day/second].
series.example: This part inside a watch ticks about 691,000 times a day.
